newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 20.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - More and more politicians and economists are leaning toward the opinion that the cabinet should quickly deregulate rents and slow down plans to increase energy prices. Experts state that deregulating rent is necessary to create a functioning market for flats, while an increase in energy prices can wait until after energy companies are privatised.

- After more than two months, compulsory administration in Ceske Narodni Investicni Spolecnost (CNIS) ended yesterday. In a meeting of the board of directors, a new management was called in to replace the state administrator, Petr Jenicek. The new management still has to be approved by the Finance Ministry.

- While at the end of last year, losses at Agrobanka, which has been under compulsory administration since last September, were estimated at around four billion crowns, Price Waterhouse now puts losses at approximately 8.7 billion crowns, twice the bank's basic capital. An Agrobanka spokesman confirmed the information but said the bank has the means to meet its obligations. Price Waterhouse declined comment.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - In the project to merge the holding companies Kaucuk Group (KG), Chemopetrol Group (ChG) and Unipetrol, the terms for the exchange of shares of the first two companies for shares of Unipetrol have been decided. For each of its shares, at a nominal value of 1,000 crowns, KG will receive 12 shares of Unipetrol, valued at 100 crowns each. One share of ChG, also valued at 1,000 crowns, will equal 11 shares of Unipetrol, also at 100 crowns.

- Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jindrich Vodicka proposed to the cabinet that Justice Minister Vlasta Parkanova should prepare a proposal for a law concerning strikes, which she must present within two weeks. Since 1991, there have been 12 strikes in the Czech Republic, and 364,321 hours were lost.

PRAVO - Toma Otrokovice, after IPB Group the largest shareholder of Svita Zlin, is dissatisfied with Svita's operations. For this reason it requested the board of directors of the company to meet on March 10, in which Toma will present a proposal for liquidating the company, according to Toma's director, Zdenek Sterba.

- The director of the National Property Fund stated that it seems that, at present, it would be most effective to liquidate Aero Holding and pay its shareholders the liquidation remainder. He added that only if the holding company can prove its viability, then there is sense in it continuing operations.

LIDOVE NOVINY - After yesterday's cabinet meeting, Environment Minister Jiri Skalicky convinced the cabinet to reject the proposal to build a new Highway D3, which should go through Prague, Tabor and Ceske Budejovice to the Austrian border.
